summary: Stores library-model nullable type-variable upper bounds in a SetMultimap instead of a Map so a class with several such type variables (e.g. BiConsumer) keeps all of them, with a regression test.

tests.evidence: Bug fix owes a regression test; JSpecifyJDKModelsTest.biConsumerNullableUpperBound makes both BiConsumer type arguments @Nullable, which fails when the Map overwrote one index. Adequate.

doc_comments.evidence: CodeRabbit asked for Javadoc on typeVariablesWithNullableUpperBounds(); a nit on an interface-implementing method, not acted on.

change_description.evidence: Description states the bug and fix; user-visible bug fix (fewer false positives) goes into NullAway's release changelog, written at release time.

backward_compat.evidence: Return type of StubxCacheUtil.getUpperBoundCache() changes, but it is an internal handlers class used only by LibraryModelsHandler.

correctness.evidence: Map<String,Integer> -> SetMultimap in StubxCacheUtil/LibraryModelsHandler; the only writer is upperBoundCache.put(className, paramIndex) (StubxCacheUtil.java:258), so the fix is mechanical.

surprising_behavior.evidence: Removes false positives for models with several nullable-bounded type variables; no new surprising behavior.

spec_conformance.evidence: JSpecify-mode JDK models; the change restores what the models already declare rather than reinterpreting the spec.

plan.why: Small, cohesive bug fix; one reviewer suffices.
